  cord_lookup_filename: "CordBloodCombined_cell_type_mean_beta.tsv"
  cibersort_filename: "Cibersort_LM22_500perm_Analysis_Tumors.csv"
  output_filename: "cohort1.analysis_tumors.methyl_adjusted.tsv"
  immune_reference: "CIBERSORTx" # "CIBERSORTx" (adult cell types weighted by CIBERSORTx), "PBMC" (one mononuclear cell profile), or "CordBlood" (cord blood cell types weighted by CIBERSORTx); the last two are saved with "_PBMC" or "_CordBlood" added to the output filename

  markdown:

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, comment = NA)
library(jsonlite)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)

source('util.R')
source(file.path(repo_dir, 'save_util.R'))

consts <- read_json(file.path(repo_dir, 'config.json'))

if (consts[["Windows"]]) {
  official_indir <- "P:"
} else {
  official_indir <- consts[['official_indir']]
}
save_path <- file.path(official_indir, params$save_path)

# Output file; the PBMC and cord blood references have their own files
stopifnot(params$immune_reference %in% c("CIBERSORTx", "PBMC", "CordBlood"))
output_filename <- params$output_filename
if (params$immune_reference != "CIBERSORTx") {
  output_filename <- sub("\\.tsv$", paste0("_", params$immune_reference, ".tsv"), output_filename)
}

# Stop now, instead of after the adjustment, if the output file already exists
if (!params$compare_existing) {
  stopIfOutputsExist(file.path(save_path, output_filename),
                     advice = "or knit with parameters and set compare_existing to TRUE to rerun and compare the results with the existing file.")
}
```

#  {.tabset}

## Data {.tabset}

### Read TARGET Methylation Data

```{r read_methylation_from_gdc}
methyl_data <- tryCatch(readRDS(file.path(save_path,
                                          paste0(params$methyl_filename, ".rds"))),
                        error = function(e) {
                          stop("must recreate the tumor methylation object")
                          })
cat("Dimensions of raw methylation data", dim(methyl_data), "\n")
```

### Restrict to Analysis Tumors

We keep only the tumors in the analysis cohort that have bulk RNA data,
which are the tumors included in the CIBERSORT analysis.

```{r restrict_to_analysis_tumors}
clinical <- read.table(file.path(save_path,
                                 params$processed_clinical_filename),
                       sep = "\t", header = TRUE)
clinical$in_analysis_dataset <- as.logical(clinical$in_analysis_dataset)
analysis_tumors <- clinical$sampleID[clinical$in_analysis_dataset]

cibersort <- read.csv(file.path(save_path,
                                params$cibersort_filename))

methyl_tumors <- getTumorIDs(colnames(methyl_data))
keep <- methyl_tumors %in% analysis_tumors &
  methyl_tumors %in% getTumorIDs(cibersort$Mixture)
methyl_data <- methyl_data[, keep]

cat("Tumors in the analysis cohort", length(analysis_tumors), "\n")
cat("Dimensions of current methylation data", dim(methyl_data), "\n")
```

### Read CIBERSORTx Results

The CIBERSORT analysis was completed for the tumors in the analysis
cohort with bulk RNA data using the LM22 signature, B-mode batch
correction, absolute mode, quantile normalization disabled, and 500
permutations.

```{r cibersort_read}
idx <- match(getTumorIDs(colnames(methyl_data)), getTumorIDs(cibersort$Mixture))
cibersort <- cibersort[idx[!is.na(idx)], ]
cat("All current tumors are contained in the CIBERSORT results",
    isTRUE(all.equal(getTumorIDs(cibersort$Mixture), getTumorIDs(colnames(methyl_data)))),
    "\n")
cat("Dimensions of CIBERSORT results", dim(cibersort), "\n")
```

### Purity Values

Purity estimates are the LUMP values in the processed clinical table.
The LUMP method is taken from Aran, D., Sirota, M. and Butte, A. J.
(2015) Systematic pan-cancer analysis of tumor purity. Nature
Communications, 6, 8971.

```{r read_purity}
# keep only the data for tumors used in the analysis
idx <- match(getTumorIDs(colnames(methyl_data)), clinical$sampleID)
purity <- data.frame("Sample.ID" = clinical$sampleID[idx],
                     "LUMP" = clinical$LUMP[idx])
cat("Dimensions of purity results", dim(purity), "\n")

cat("All current tumors are in the purity dataset:",
    isTRUE(all.equal(purity$Sample.ID, getTumorIDs(colnames(methyl_data)))), "\n")
```

## Adjust $\beta$ Values {.tabset}

#### Definition

For each tumor, the purity-adjusted beta value of the tumor cells at CpG
site $k$, $\beta_{k}^{t}$, is defined as

$$
\beta_{k}^{t} = \frac{1}{p}\left[\beta_{k}^{m} - (1 - p) ~ \beta^{imp}_{k}\right],
$$

where $p$ is the tumor's purity (LUMP), $\beta_{k}^{m}$ is the measured
beta value at CpG site $k$, and $\beta_{k}^{imp}$ is the beta value of
the infiltrating immune cells at site $k$, estimated as

$$
\beta^{imp}_{k} = \sum_{l = 1}^{22} \frac{s_{l} * \beta_{l,k}}{S}.
$$

Here, $s_{l}$ is the absolute score of the $l^{th}$ LM22 cell type and
$S$ is the tumor's absolute score (the sum of the 22 cell-type scores),
both from the CIBERSORTx analysis, so the weights $s_{l}/S$ sum to 1.
$\beta_{l,k}$ is the average methylation at site $k$ of the blood cell
type in the WBC lookup table that LM22 cell type $l$ is mapped to (see
the mapping below). Adjusted values outside $[0, 1]$ are truncated.

With `immune_reference` set to "PBMC", $\beta_{k}^{imp}$ is instead the
average methylation at site $k$ of peripheral blood mononuclear cells
(PBMC) in the WBC lookup table, the same for every tumor, without the
CIBERSORTx cell-type weights.

With `immune_reference` set to "CordBlood", $\beta_{l,k}$ is instead taken
from a lookup table of sorted cord blood cell types
(FlowSorted.CordBloodCombined.450k; Gervin et al., 2019), made by
*Cord_Blood_Lookup_Table.R*, with the same CIBERSORTx weights. Cord blood
has no separate neutrophils or eosinophils, so the LM22 cell types mapped
to them are mapped to cord blood granulocytes.

#### Beta Value Lookup

The WBC lookup table holds the average beta value of each purified blood
cell type at each CpG site in GEO series GSE35069 (Reinius et al., 2012),
across its 6 donors. It is made by *WBC_Lookup_Table.ipynb*.

```{r read_wbc_lookup}
# the lookup table is in the "Other" directory of official_indir
lookup_filename <- if (params$immune_reference == "CordBlood") params$cord_lookup_filename else params$lookup_filename
lookup <- read.table(file.path(official_indir, "Other", lookup_filename),
                     sep = "\t", header = TRUE, check.names = FALSE)
cat("Lookup table:", lookup_filename, "\n")

# keep only the CpG sites of interest
idx <- match(rownames(methyl_data), lookup$ID_REF)
if (any(is.na(idx))) stop("CpG sites don't match up")

lookup <- lookup[idx, ]
cat("All selected CpG sites are present",
    isTRUE(all.equal(lookup$ID_REF, rownames(methyl_data))), "\n")
```

Manipulate these results into the structure of CIBERSORTx.

```{r convert_table_to_LM22}
B.cells <- c("B.cells.memory", "Plasma.cells",
             "B.cells.naive")
Macro <- c("Macrophages.M2", "Macrophages.M0",
           "Dendritic.cells.activated", "Monocytes",
           "Macrophages.M1", "Dendritic.cells.resting")
Mast <- c("Eosinophils", "Mast.cells.activated", "Mast.cells.resting")
Myeloid <- c("Neutrophils")
NK <- c("NK.cells.resting", "NK.cells.activated")
T.CD8.cells <- c("T.cells.gamma.delta", "T.cells.CD8")
T.CD4.cells <- c("T.cells.follicular.helper", "T.cells.CD4.naive",
                 "T.cells.regulatory..Tregs.", "T.cells.CD4.memory.activated",
                 "T.cells.CD4.memory.resting")

# align these with the headers from the WBC datafile
grouping_adult <- list("CD4+ T cells" = T.CD4.cells,
                       "CD8+ T cells" = T.CD8.cells,
                       "CD14+ Monocytes" = Macro,
                       "CD19+ B cells" = B.cells,
                       "CD56+ NK cells" = NK,
                       "Eosinophils" = Mast,
                       "Neutrophils" = Myeloid)

# cord blood has granulocytes, but no separate eosinophils or neutrophils
grouping_cord <- c(grouping_adult[setdiff(names(grouping_adult), c("Eosinophils", "Neutrophils"))],
                   list("Granulocytes" = c(Mast, Myeloid)))

grouping_to_wbc <- if (params$immune_reference == "CordBlood") grouping_cord else grouping_adult
cat("All cell types are present in lookup",
    all(names(grouping_to_wbc) %in% colnames(lookup)), "\n")
cat("All cell types are present in cibersort",
    all(unlist(grouping_to_wbc) %in% colnames(cibersort)), "\n")

idx <- sapply(seq_along(grouping_to_wbc),
              function(i) rep(names(grouping_to_wbc)[i],
                              length(grouping_to_wbc[[i]]))) |> unlist()
lookup_lm22 <- lookup[, idx]
colnames(lookup_lm22) <- unlist(grouping_to_wbc)
lookup_lm22 <- data.matrix(lookup_lm22)
rownames(lookup_lm22) <- lookup$ID_REF

tst <- NULL
for (i in 1L:length(grouping_to_wbc)) {
  for (j in 1L:length(grouping_to_wbc[[i]])) {
    tst <- c(tst, isTRUE(all.equal(unlist(lookup[, names(grouping_to_wbc)[i]]),
                                   lookup_lm22[, grouping_to_wbc[[i]][j]],
                                   check.attributes = FALSE)))
  }
}
cat("This realignment worked:", all(tst), "\n")
```

#### Cell Type Mapping Table

The mapping of the LM22 cell types to the cell types of the adult (GSE35069)
and cord blood lookup tables is saved as an Excel table in the "Other"
directory of official_indir. It is the same for every `immune_reference`
(the PBMC reference doesn't use it).

```{r save_cell_type_mapping}
# LM22 cell types in the order of the CIBERSORTx results
lm22_types <- intersect(colnames(cibersort), unlist(grouping_adult))
stopifnot(setequal(lm22_types, unlist(grouping_adult)),
          setequal(lm22_types, unlist(grouping_cord)))

# lookup table cell type that each LM22 cell type is mapped to
mapTo <- function(grouping) {
  sapply(lm22_types, function(x) names(grouping)[sapply(grouping, function(g) x %in% g)])
}

# LM22 names as CIBERSORTx writes them (R turned spaces and parentheses into dots)
lm22_names <- gsub("\\.", " ", sub("\\.\\.Tregs\\.$", " (Tregs)", lm22_types))

cell_type_mapping <- data.frame("LM22 cell type" = lm22_names,
                                "Adult reference (GSE35069)" = mapTo(grouping_adult),
                                "Cord blood reference (FlowSorted.CordBloodCombined.450k)" = mapTo(grouping_cord),
                                check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
knitr::kable(cell_type_mapping)

writeWithoutOverwrite(
  file.path(official_indir, "Other", "LM22_cell_type_mapping.xlsx"),
  cell_type_mapping,
  writeFunc = function(filepath, data) writexl::write_xlsx(data, filepath),
  readFunc = function(filepath) as.data.frame(readxl::read_excel(filepath)),
  compareFunc = function(data, existing_data) {
    identical(colnames(data), colnames(existing_data)) &&
      isTRUE(all.equal(data, existing_data, check.attributes = FALSE))
  }
)
```

#### Plot distributions of absolute proportions of immune cell types

```{r plot_cibersort_proportions, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6}
components <- as.character(unlist(grouping_to_wbc))

# One row per tumor and cell type
cibersort_long <- cibersort[, c("Mixture", components)] %>%
  pivot_longer(-Mixture, names_to = "cell_type", values_to = "proportion") %>%
  mutate(
    cell_type = trimws(gsub("\\.+", " ", cell_type)),            # e.g. T.cells.CD8 -> T cells CD8
    cell_type = reorder(cell_type, proportion, FUN = median)     # order cell types by median proportion
  )

ggplot(cibersort_long, aes(x = proportion, y = cell_type)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.8) +
  labs(x = "Absolute proportion (CIBERSORTx)", y = NULL,
       title = sprintf("Immune cell types in %d tumors", nrow(cibersort))) +
  theme_classic()
```

#### Calculate site specific beta values

```{r calculate_weight}
# align the cell type columns
idx <- match(colnames(cibersort[, 2L:23L]), colnames(lookup_lm22))
if (any(is.na(idx))) stop("cell types do not match")

# reorder lookup table to match ordering of cibersort results
lookup_lm22 <- lookup_lm22[, idx]
cat("columns of cibersort align with lookup_lm22",
    isTRUE(all.equal(colnames(cibersort)[2L:23L], colnames(lookup_lm22))), "\n")
cat("tumor names of cibersort align with methyl_data",
    isTRUE(all.equal(getTumorIDs(cibersort$Mixture),
                     getTumorIDs(colnames(methyl_data)))), "\n")

# calculate beta_i^imp
lm22_wgts <- matrix(0.0, nrow = nrow(methyl_data), ncol = ncol(methyl_data))
for (i in 1L:ncol(methyl_data)) {
  tumor_index <- which(getTumorIDs(cibersort$Mixture) == getTumorIDs(colnames(methyl_data)[i]))
  cs_tumor <- cibersort[tumor_index, 2L:23L]
  lm22_wgts[, i] <- {lookup_lm22 %*% t(data.matrix(cs_tumor))} / cibersort$Absolute.score..sig.score.[tumor_index]
}

# PBMC reference: the same mononuclear cell profile for every tumor
if (params$immune_reference == "PBMC") {
  lm22_wgts <- matrix(lookup$PBMC, nrow = nrow(methyl_data), ncol = ncol(methyl_data))
}
cat("Immune cell reference:", params$immune_reference, "\n")
```

```{r generate_and_save}
beta_adj1_tumor <- {{t(methyl_data) - t(lm22_wgts) * {1.0 - purity$LUMP}} / purity$LUMP} |> t()

cat("This adjustment results in ", mean(beta_adj1_tumor < 0.0 | beta_adj1_tumor > 1.0, na.rm = TRUE)*100,
    "% of the non-NA beta values outside of [0, 1]; we truncate these.\n")
# truncation to physical values
beta_adj1_tumor <- pmin(pmax(beta_adj1_tumor, 0.0), 1.0)

# Save, but don't overwrite an existing file that has different values
writeWithoutOverwrite(
  file.path(save_path, output_filename),
  beta_adj1_tumor,
  writeFunc = function(filepath, data) write.table(data, file = filepath, sep = "\t"),
  readFunc = function(filepath) data.matrix(read.table(filepath, sep = "\t", header = TRUE,
                                                       check.names = FALSE)),
  # Same sites and tumors, and the same values (missing in the same places)
  compareFunc = function(data, existing_data) {
    identical(dimnames(data), dimnames(existing_data)) &&
      isTRUE(all.equal(data, existing_data, tolerance = 1e-6, check.attributes = FALSE))
  }
)
```
